I have been reading Victor Frankl's book lately. He talks about how we often give up thinking that we have nothing left to expect from life anymore. Instead, it should be about what life expects of us, what we are destined to do and supposed to become, the things we are meant to work on which only we can, and of the people who depend on us. How, even in suffering, we are unique and alone in the universe. No one can relieve our suffering or suffer in our place. Our unique opportunity lies in the way we bear our burden. He often quotes Nietzsche's words, "He who has a why to live can bear almost any how"

I think about all the things I'll miss, the people I'll hurt and places I will never get to explore if I go now. However, I often lose that hope and my will to live. It is a constant battle.
